The strikes reduce Russian refining capacity and contribute to rising US diesel prices.
Kyiv argues it must target infrastructure while Russia bombards Ukrainian cities.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ukraine struck an oil facility in Russia’s Samara region, a Russian vessel in the Black Sea, and a drone site in Oryol. Donald Trump urged Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt refinery attacks, blaming them for global diesel shortages and rising US fuel prices.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Kyiv is unlikely to stop targeting Russian oil infrastructure while Moscow continues its daily attacks. Russia has extended its diesel export ban until the end of October.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Senate Democrats blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act on Wednesday. The measure failed to reach the sixty votes required to pass, receiving fifty-seven votes in favour and forty-three against. Four Democrats voted alongside Republicans to support the bill, which the House of Representatives had previously approved nearly unanimously.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Lawmakers introduced the proposal to address voter worries regarding rising electricity bills caused by growing datacenter construction. Senate Democrats opposed the bill because they viewed it as ineffective, while critics argued the vote created a difficult political dilemma regarding living costs ahead of the midterm elections.
